THE SPLIT OUTRAN THE EXCLUSION, and it is why main went red on 2026-09-06. capture-core.mjs was excluded because it drives NVDA. On 2026-09-05 it was split into three, and the exclusion followed only the PARENT - so 4,823 statements of guidepup-driving code entered the measured population at 0%, and packages/ fell from 87.18% to 77.64%. Nothing in the split was wrong and no test was deleted.

THAT IS THIS REPOSITORY'S MOST EXPENSIVE RECURRING SHAPE, arriving in its own coverage config: a remedy applied at one call site when the behaviour reaches several - the defect capture-core.mjs's own header catalogues four times. WHEN A FILE IN THIS LIST IS SPLIT, EVERY CHILD INHERITS ITS REASON OR EARNS AN EXPLICIT ONE.

A COVERAGE THRESHOLD IS A SHARED BUDGET. One untestable file spends everyone's, and the cost lands on whoever pushes next - here, on a main that six PRs were queued behind. The floor is not lowered to fit a file; the file is either made testable, or excluded with its reason stated here.

RE-DERIVED AGAIN BY THE SAME METHOD, 2026-10-07 (#3993), because the POPULATION changed, not because a number was lowered to fit. The packages left (lab, control, agent-org, and nvda-worker/worker-fleet as laid `src/` with their tests in their own repositories), and 73/72 was a reading of a tree that held their tests. Measured at e31b5ec69 plus #3991, `pnpm run coverage` in a fresh worktree: 33.11% lines / 33.38% statements over 12,717 lines, of which 4,094 + 1,618 statements were the two laid layers above (0% and 2.3%). With those two excluded: lines 4,179/8,041 = 51.97%, statements 5,239/10,090 = 51.92% -> 51/51. The fresh-worktree reading was not the cause: the unfolded child coverage (10 files, 9 statements) and the `[eval1]` ENOENT are worth under 0.1 point, and the child-process fold adds 1.1.

RATCHETED 51/51 -> 70/69 BY THE SAME METHOD, 2026-10-07 (#3998), because tests landed for the files above, not because anything was excluded. Of the 109 files that read 0% in the baseline report (root `scripts/*.mjs`, `packages/guards/src/*.mjs`), 19 now have a test of their own, and 20 fewer read 0% (`packages/guards/src/<name>.test.ts`, the only glob the gates run: a `scripts/*.test.ts` is picked up by none of them). Measured with `pnpm run coverage` in a fresh worktree at 5768e1d44 plus those tests, 0 failing: merged lines 5,687/8,003 = 71.06%, statements 7,465/10,642 = 70.14% locally, but the CI runner (the environment that gates) read lines 70.71%, statements 69.36% on the same tree (run 37659315729), 0.35 and 0.78 points lower for reasons not isolated, so the floor of the CI reading is the threshold -> 70/69. The local baseline at the same head was lines 4,179/8,003 = 52.21%, statements 5,239/10,047 = 52.14%. The statement TOTAL grew by 595 because rstest counts a file by its AST until a test loads it and by v8 blocks after, so part of the rise is a re-measurement of files that were already covered in name only, and the figure is a reading of this tree, not a promise about the next.

NATIVELY LOADED TYPESCRIPT IS UNMEASURABLE HERE, SO 17 FILES ARE EXCLUDED BY NAME (#4393). Renaming the held-back `.mjs` to `.ts` made `@rstest/coverage-v8`'s parser read raw TypeScript for any file Node loads by itself (the worker's `--import` preload `walk-scope`, the ESLint plugin's rules, a spawned `node file.ts`) instead of one rspack transpiled: `Failed to process coverage ... SyntaxError`, which sets the exit code of the rstest child and failed `ts / run` with 2,647 tests passing. The `.mjs` they were parsed fine. Excluding a file is the only thing that stops the failure (a file is parsed whether or not `include` names it), and each is excluded because no test CAN read it with this provider, not because it is untested. The 12 renamed scripts are named in `include` one by one, not as `scripts/*.ts`, because the root `scripts/` already holds `.ts` files that were never in this population and a glob would have admitted them (measured: 62.16/62.41 with the glob and the failures, 70.27/70.76 with the glob and the exclusions, 81.72/81.19 with the named list and the exclusions, `pnpm run coverage` at 57bb9154a plus this edit).

WHAT IS LOST: these 17 are out of the denominator and out of the numerator, so the 81.72/81.19 reading is of a smaller population than the 79/76.8 main read at 7f9a606d4. The 17 (`local-import-closure` left for `@a11ign/toolchain` in #4718): packages/guards/src/{changed-files,changed-packages,git-env,git-spawn-scrubbed,isolation-gate,mutation-check,piped-exit-status-guard,uncontrolled-emptiness,walk-scope}.ts and scripts/{agent-org-newest-tag,ci-changed,cli-flags,lay-layer,npm-cli-executable,private-tmp,refuse-other-installers,registry-consumer-gate}.ts. A later toolchain that parses type-stripped TypeScript should delete these lines and be re-measured.
